# Largest Positive Integer That Exists With Its Negative.

@example There is no -9 for the 9; 5 and 2 both have their opposites, and 5 is the larger.
[5,-2,9,-5,2]
=> 5

@example -8 has no 8, so the only mirrored number is 3.
[-8,3,-3,1]
=> 3

@example No number here has its opposite.
[4,7,-1,-5]
=> -1

# A single element is never mirrored.
[7]
=> -1

[-1000]
=> -1

# The smallest and the largest possible mirrored numbers.
[-1,1]
=> 1

[1000,-1000]
=> 1000

# The largest value present only as a negative: the answer is not 1000.
[-1000,3,-3]
=> 3

# The largest positive has no partner, but a smaller one does.
[1000,-999,999]
=> 999

# Every value positive, with repeats.
[2,2,2,3]
=> -1

# Every value negative.
[-1,-2,-3]
=> -1

# Both signs, but no magnitude appears with both.
[1,-2,3,-4]
=> -1

# Several mirrored numbers: the largest wins, whatever the order.
[-9,1,2,3,9,-1]
=> 9

[6,-6,2,-2,4,-4]
=> 6

# The first pair met in a left-to-right scan (2) and the last one (4) are
# both smaller than 7.
[2,-7,-2,4,7,-4]
=> 7

# Repeated copies of a mirrored number count once; 5 has no -5.
[-4,-4,4,4,4,5,5]
=> 4

# The two opposites at the two ends.
[-7,1,2,3,4,5,6,8,7]
=> 7

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[-1,-1,-1,-1,1,1,-1]
=> 1

@gen 2 small
[-1000,998,-999,-998,-999]
=> 998

@gen 3 small
[998,1000,996,997,998,-998,999,-996]
=> 998

@gen 4 small
[-2,-5,-4,-3]
=> -1

@gen 5 small
[2,-1,2,2,2,-1]
=> -1

@gen 6 small
[3,1]
=> -1

@gen 7 small
[-2,-3,3,-3,-3,3]
=> 3
